aAbout: ADS-B Exchange is a global platform that aggregates and displays real-time aircraft movements via a collaborative network of contributors, offering a transparent view of the skies without censorship or filtering. Its live Global Map shows all aircraft broadcasts as received — military, commercial and private — fed by what it claims is a network of over 25,000 active receivers, with a map history function going back to March 2020. Alongside the map it sells production-ready enterprise data subscriptions (live and daily position and operations feeds); no enterprise prices are published.
aStrengths: ADS-B Exchange is the deeper archive of the two: a map history function reaching back to March 2020, detailed aircraft and ownership information, premium map layers and aeronautical charts, and — by its own claim — positions refreshing every 500ms from over 25,000 receivers. It is also the one with a business behind the map: enterprise live and daily data products for customers who need the feed itself, not just the picture.
bAbout: Airplanes.live is a community-run ADS-B aggregator: receivers built and hosted by enthusiasts pick up ADS-B and MLAT signals from the aircraft overhead, and the combined feed shows what is flying right now. It states it will never filter or obfuscate aircraft data — including military aircraft, aircraft squawking an emergency and LADD-enrolled aircraft other trackers suppress. It was founded by four aviation enthusiasts, is not run for profit, and its by-laws say the organisation cannot be sold, transferred or taken over by any one individual. The web map is free permanently, with an official iOS app alongside it.
bStrengths: Airplanes.live is the purer community proposition: an unfiltered map that is free permanently, with no accounts, no ads and — by its app site's account — no trackers or third-party analytics. Its official iOS app adds what ADS-B Exchange's web map does not confirm: an ATC scope mode, advanced filters, an unlimited watchlist on Pro, and push alerts for followed aircraft and 7700 emergency squawks. Feeders get Pro free for as long as they keep feeding.
betterAnswer: On the headline promise — an unfiltered sky — they are tied: both show military and LADD traffic and neither filters. The split is everything around it. ADS-B Exchange is the researcher's tool: history back to March 2020, ownership detail, enterprise feeds and a claimed 25,000+ receiver network, paid for with an ad-supported free map. Airplanes.live is the purist's tool: free forever, no accounts, no ads, and the alerts and scope mode live in its iOS app. Pick by whether you need the archive or the app.

intro: ADS-B Exchange and Airplanes.live are the two community trackers that refuse to filter the sky — and they agree on almost nothing else. ADS-B Exchange, founded in 2016, pairs its unfiltered Global Map with a history function back to March 2020, an ad-free personal subscription and enterprise data products with no public prices. Airplanes.live, founded by four aviation enthusiasts as a not-for-profit that its by-laws say cannot be sold, keeps its web map free permanently with no accounts and no ads, and puts its paid tier inside an official iOS app. Both show the military and LADD traffic commercial trackers suppress; what differs is the model around the map.
pricingA: The live Global Map is free with ads. The personal ad-free subscription costs $2.99/month or $29.95/year — for individual, personal use only, with premium map layers — and feeders get the ad-free map free. Enterprise data subscriptions (Live positions, Live operations, Daily positions, Daily operations) have no public price: ADS-B Exchange does not publish one, so any figure quoted elsewhere should not be trusted.
pricingB: The web map is free — Airplanes.live's app site states the unfiltered map is free, permanently, and no web subscription price is published. The official iOS app is freemium: Free at $0 (the full unfiltered live map, aircraft details, photos and routes, search, and no ads), and Pro at $2.99/month or $19.99/year, adding live weather radar, ATC scope mode and convergence alerts, advanced filters, an unlimited watchlist and push alerts. Pro is free for active feeders for as long as they keep feeding.

verdictA: Choose ADS-B Exchange if the archive is the point — history back to March 2020, ownership detail and enterprise-grade feeds — and you accept ads on the free map or a small personal subscription to remove them.
verdictB: Choose Airplanes.live if the principle is the point — a free-forever, account-free, ad-free unfiltered map — and especially if you are on iPhone, where its Pro alerts and scope mode live.
verdictLine: Both refuse to filter the sky; they part on everything else. ADS-B Exchange is the archive with a business attached — deep history and enterprise data behind an ad-supported map. Airplanes.live is the commons — free, account-free and ad-free, with its best extras in an iOS app.
worldEye: If you want the sky in context rather than the sky alone, WorldEye shows live flights free on a 3D globe — no signup — alongside live ships, satellites, weather, earthquakes, wildfires and 74,229 public cameras across 109 countries in the same view. It is deliberately not a rival to either community tracker here: it does not claim their unfiltered military data, and it does not offer ADS-B Exchange's history back to 2020. An optional Pro tier ($7.99/week, $13.99/month or $74.99/year) adds the OSINT toolkit and intel feeds.
